reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read all six scenes, five vocabulary entries, the pause question, two discussion questions, alt texts, content note, provenance and adaptation changes in full against the full Ryder text, and re-read and approved the corrected text.

Safeguarding fix before approval: the source's boy shut in a cave behind a rock, presented in the first draft as a game, was replaced by the boy spending the afternoon with the merchant's own sister, a known adult; changes and the parent note say exactly this and suggest a safety talk with children.

Cause and effect follow Ryder: the balance left in trust, the 'mice ate it' lie, the 'hawk carried him' answer, the magistrates' laughter, and both the balance and the boy returned. Frame verified: Cheek tells Victor in Book I.
The pause question precedes the plan; discussion question 1 asks whether frightening Lakshman was fair. No em dashes.
2026-10-05: the coordinator changed only the age label from 8–12 to 8+ under the new age bands (2+, 8+, 10+, 12+, 16+); no story text changed, so the text approval above still applies.
illustrations: Panels 1 and 6: the same large black iron beam balance with two chained pans, handed over and returned.
Panel 3: the boy eats happily on an open veranda with Naduk's sister beside him and Naduk talking with her; no cave, no confinement, never alone.
Panel 4: one distant hawk with empty talons; Naduk points up with mock concern and Lakshman protests. Panel 5: laughing judges, Naduk explaining, Lakshman's head bowed.
Lakshman is shown with dignity and an ordinary build throughout; neither merchant is caricatured. A small hand scale on the shop wall in panels 1 and 2 is a separate object.
Grid seams exactly at x=512 and y=512/1024; no lettering, no modern objects. Accepted minor issues: panel 6 shows the moment after the handover, and the boy reads a little younger than twelve.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age suitability has not been tested with children; apparent ages in the art are subjective readings.
Source fidelity was checked against the full rendered Wikisource text of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.
Art was judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with pixel measurement of the grid; not every scene was checked in the app's dark mode.
